messages:
raj: Hey team — we're getting an escalation from a customer (org_id=org_9f2) where users are forced to re-auth right after completing MFA. Happens across devices and browsers. Customer says it started after last weekend's deployment. They see immediate signout on any protected route.

emma: Thanks @raj. Can you paste repro steps and any request ids? Also which environment (prod/dedicated)?

raj: repro steps 
1) Login via SSO (Okta) -> complete MFA (push)
2) Redirect to app -> app immediately 302s to /login
3) Cookies present in browser devtools but session is gone.
Environment: prod (hosted). Example request id: req_0a12f3.

emma: Got it. Can you capture the Set-Cookie header for the login response and the subsequent requests?

raj: Pasted headers from the login response:
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Domain=app.example.com
Set-Cookie: SRV-AFF=abcd; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; Max-Age=3600
Location: https://app.example.com/
```
And then the next request from browser includes Cookie: SRV-AFF=abcd; but session is not sent (or browser drops it).

maya: Max-Age=0 + explicit Expires in the past — that will immediately expire the cookie. Where is that Max-Age coming from?

raj: Exactly. But the login flow used to set Max-Age=1209600. Changed behavior since Sunday. Customer says multiple users got re-auth prompts.

sam: tagging infra: @infra-oncall have we rolled anything that touches session rotation or the login proxy? Also check if CDN/edge is rewriting Set-Cookie. We had a small change to the session rotate code in commit 3f7d2c last week (auth: set cookie via helper).

infra-oncall: We deployed a tiny patch to auth-proxy on 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC. The patch touched Set-Cookie generation in order to unify SameSite handling. Rollout history: canary -> 10% -> 100% around 03:37. No other infra changes.

emma: Raj, can you curl the login callback from our edge (to check raw headers) and paste output? Example curl we use:
```
curl -i -L 'https://auth-edge.example.com/callback?code=XXX' -H 'Host: app.example.com'
```

raj: output snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Domain=app.example.com
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=1209600; Domain=.example.com
```
Weird — two Set-Cookie lines for session. One with Max-Age=0 and Domain=app.example.com, another with normal Max-Age and Domain=.example.com. Browser apparently picks the more specific one (app.example.com) which has Max-Age=0, so it deletes the cookie.

sam: aha — duplicate Set-Cookie with conflicting attributes. Probably the auth service sets cookie for the public domain ('.example.com') and the edge proxy also re-sets it for the host with Max-Age=0 (bug).

maya: Could this be due to our recent helper setting a default Max-Age when cookie value empty? If edge is re-issuing a blank cookie as part of cleanup, it might set Max-Age=0 intentionally but it's running in the wrong codepath.

deploy-bot: Affected service: auth-proxy. Recent commits: 3f7d2c (auth: unify samesite), 3f7d2c+1 (auth: cookie cleanup). Rollback candidate: revert 3f7d2c+1.

emma: Sam, can you grep the code for any call that sets Max-Age=0 on session cookie?

sam: Found it. In auth-proxy/session.go there is a function clearCookie(w) which does: 
```
http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{Name: "session", Value: "", Path: "/", Domain: r.Host, HttpOnly: true, Secure: true, MaxAge: 0})
```
That function is invoked on an error branch that should only run on signout, but earlier refactor changed when the branch executes after SSO callback error. For some SSO success flows the proxy erroneously goes through the cleanup path then still writes the real cookie. Order of Set-Cookie means host-specific Max-Age=0 wins.

emma: Nice catch. So root cause: logic reordering in 3f7d2c+1 causing clearCookie to run before writing the canonical cookie. Patch idea: ensure clearCookie only runs if we will abort the response, or write canonical cookie with same domain+path last.

raj: Customer impacted: org_9f2, ~120 active users across regions. They've already rotated keys and said they'll escalate to legal if not fixed quickly.

infra-oncall: Hotfix plan: 1) revert 3f7d2c+1 from auth-proxy at 1895004080 (canary) 2) redeploy canary, verify with curl that single Set-Cookie present 3) roll as 10/100.

sam: Working on patch now. Minimal change: stop calling clearCookie during callback, and add unit test asserting final Set-Cookie attributes. Pushing PR 3f7d2c+2.

emma: After we patch, can we reach out to the customer with a short repro and mitigation? They can tell users to clear cookies but that's not acceptable at scale. We'll aim for rollback/hotfix within the hour.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for auth-proxy revision 3f7d2c+1 -> reverting to 3f7d2c. Canary deployment started (id: can_1895).

sam: Canary shows single Set-Cookie now: 
```
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=1209600; Domain=.example.com
```
Verified with chrome and curl.

raj: Confirmed with customer — behavior fixed for now. They still saw some stale sessions that required manual cookie clear but new logins work.

maya: Follow-ups: add linter test to disallow writing two Set-Cookie for same name in one response; add integration test with sso callback flow. Also add telemetry: emit metric when clearCookie is called during callback flow.

emma: I'll file a support follow-up and schedule a postmortem if needed. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
